1.title: Quick-Reference Recap
1.text: Welcome to Module 17: Quick-Reference Recap. This is the course on a few pages, for the last two days before the exam. There is one page for each topic module, then the numbers to know, and the key terms. Use it to test yourself: look at a page, cover the text, and say the facts aloud before you listen to them.

1.title: Module 1: Scrum Definition, Theory and Empiricism
1.text: Module one in one page. Scrum is a lightweight framework for value from complex work. Its theory is empiricism and lean thinking. The pillars are transparency, inspection and adaptation, in a chain. The approach is iterative and incremental. Partial Scrum is not Scrum. And empirical process control is the earlier edition's wording.

1.title: Module 2: Scrum Values and the Agile Manifesto
1.text: Module two in one page. The five values are commitment, focus, openness, respect and courage. They give direction and make the pillars real. The Manifesto has four values and twelve principles. Left over right, but the right side keeps its value. Match an idea to a Scrum feature: the Increment with working software, the emergent Product Backlog with change, the Retrospective with reflection. The Manifesto is a mindset; Scrum is a framework.

1.title: Module 3: The Scrum Team and the Developers
1.text: Module three in one page. A Scrum Master, a Product Owner, and Developers. No sub-teams and no hierarchy. Typically ten or fewer people. Cross-functional means collective skills, and self-managing means deciding who does what. The whole team answers for the Increment. The Developers are accountable for the Sprint plan, quality, daily adaptation and mutual accountability.

1.title: Module 4: The Product Owner
1.text: Module four in one page. The Product Owner is accountable for the value of the product and for Product Backlog management. A single person; the work may be delegated, the accountability stays. Stakeholders convince, and the organization respects the decisions. The Developers size and select. The Product Owner alone cancels a Sprint. And at the Daily Scrum, the Product Owner takes part only as a Developer.

1.title: Module 5: The Scrum Master
1.text: Module five in one page. The Scrum Master is accountable for Scrum itself and for the team's effectiveness, as a true leader who serves. The Scrum Master serves the team, the Product Owner and the organization. The Daily Scrum is the Developers' event. Decisions stay with their owners. And the best answer serves, makes the problem visible, keeps Scrum intact, and acts. The diagram recalls the three audiences the Scrum Master serves.

1.title: Module 6: The Sprint and the Scrum Events
1.text: Module six in one page. The Sprint is fixed, one month or less, and it is the container. Five events: the Sprint plus four. The maximums for a one-month Sprint are eight hours, fifteen minutes, four hours and three hours. The Review is second to last, and the Retrospective concludes the Sprint. Shorter Sprints limit risk. And Sprint zero, hardening Sprints and extending a Sprint are not Scrum.

1.title: Module 7: Sprint Planning
1.text: Module seven in one page. Three topics: why, what and how. The output is the Sprint Backlog: goal, items and plan. The whole Scrum Team plans. The Developers select the items and decide how. Eight hours at most for a one-month Sprint. And an estimation technique is not in the Guide.

1.title: Module 8: Daily Scrum
1.text: Module eight in one page. The purpose is to check progress toward the Sprint Goal and adjust the plan. Fifteen minutes, every working day, at a fixed time and place. It is the Developers' event, and they choose the structure. The output is a plan for the next day. It is not a status meeting.

1.title: Module 9: Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective
1.text: Module nine in one page. The Review inspects the outcome with key stakeholders, adapts the Product Backlog, and takes four hours at most. The Retrospective inspects the way of working, with the Scrum Team, plans improvements, and takes three hours at most. The Review is never a gate. What is not Done is not shown. And skipping the Retrospective means problems repeat.

1.title: Module 10: Product Backlog, Product Goal and Refinement
1.text: Module ten in one page. The Product Backlog is emergent, ordered, and the single source of work. The commitments are the Product Goal, the Sprint Goal and the Definition of Done. An item has a description, an order and a size. Ready means it can be Done within one Sprint. Refinement is ongoing and not an event. And one Product Goal at a time.

1.title: Module 11: Sprint Backlog and Sprint Goal
1.text: Module eleven in one page. The Sprint Backlog is the goal, the items and the plan, and it belongs to the Developers. It is updated all through the Sprint. The Sprint Goal is one objective and a commitment. The plan and the scope may change; the goal and the quality may not. Scope is negotiated with the Product Owner. And an obsolete goal lets the Product Owner cancel.

1.title: Module 12: Increment and Definition of Done
1.text: Module twelve in one page. An Increment is usable, additive, and thoroughly verified. It is born when an item meets the Definition of Done. Several can arise in a Sprint, and the Review is no gate. The Definition of Done gives a shared understanding, and the Developers conform to it. The organization's standard is the minimum. And teams on one product share one.

1.title: Module 13: Facilitation, Teaching, Mentoring and Coaching
1.text: Module thirteen in one page. Facilitating is neutral on content and active on process. The techniques: dot voting, Roman voting, Fist of Five, one-two-four-all, consensus and majority vote. Teaching and mentoring: the Scrum Master shares. Coaching: the coachee answers. And the test question: who has the answer?

1.title: Module 14: Impediments, Technical Debt and the Organization
1.text: Module fourteen in one page. For impediments: make them visible, find the root cause, resolve with the right people, and verify. There are team and organizational levels. Techniques: five whys, fishbone, a board, and escalation with data. Debt makes delivery slower, costlier and riskier, and the Definition of Done guards against it. Practices: automated testing, continuous integration and refactoring. And there is no project manager.

1.title: Numbers to Know (1): The Framework
1.text: The numbers of the framework. The Scrum Team has a Scrum Master, a Product Owner and Developers, typically ten or fewer people. Three accountabilities. Five events: the Sprint plus four. Three artifacts, each with one commitment: the Product Goal, the Sprint Goal and the Definition of Done. Three pillars: transparency, inspection and adaptation. Five values, in this order: commitment, focus, openness, respect, courage. Keep these counts apart.

1.title: Numbers to Know (2): Time and Rules
1.text: The numbers of time and rules. A Sprint is one month or less, fixed, and the next one starts at once. Sprint Planning: eight hours at most for a one-month Sprint, with three topics. The Daily Scrum: fifteen minutes, every working day. The Sprint Review: four hours at most. The Retrospective: three hours at most, and it concludes the Sprint. Work items are often one day or less. The Product Owner is one person, and the only one who cancels a Sprint. One Product Goal at a time. And the exam: fifty questions, sixty minutes, thirty-seven correct.

1.title: Key Terms (1): A to I
1.text: Key terms, first half. Read the table at your own pace; I will point out the pairs that are easy to confuse. An artifact represents work or value, while an event is a formal chance to inspect and adapt. Inspection is checking, and adaptation is adjusting. The Definition of Done is the quality bar of the Increment, and it is that artifact's commitment. And the Developers are everyone who builds the Increment, not just programmers.

1.title: Key Terms (2): L to T
1.text: Key terms, second half. Again, look for the pairs. The Product Goal is the long-term target and belongs to the Product Backlog. The Sprint Goal is one Sprint's objective and belongs to the Sprint Backlog. The Product Backlog is the list of everything needed; the Sprint Backlog is the Developers' plan for one Sprint. Technical debt is not in the Guide, so know it by its effects. And remember a timebox is a maximum, never a target.
